strengths: The paper addresses an important question: why adversarial training can preserve clean generalization while exhibiting a large robust generalization gap. Studying these outcomes jointly is well motivated.

The decomposition into shared signal learning and example-specific noise memorization provides an interpretable candidate mechanism. Combining representation complexity with training dynamics could offer useful insights.
The manuscript includes MNIST, CIFAR10, synthetic experiments, and additional loss-landscape diagnostics. These provide concrete observations motivating the proposed explanation.
weaknesses: Theorem 4.4 is false under its stated assumptions. Consider equal probability on ±e1, radius δ = 1/4, and the small ReLU classifier fclean(x) = 0.1 − |x1 − 1|. This satisfies Assumptions 4.1–4.3: clean error is zero and robust error is 1/2. With N growing, both support points appear frequently; vanishing robust training error then forces zero robust test error. Consequently, no CGRO classifier exists. Additional assumptions controlling sample coverage and remaining population vulnerability are essential.

The construction supporting Theorem 4.4 also has independent proof errors. Assumption 4.2 separates opposite classes, but does not make same-class training balls disjoint, so replacing the union indicator with a sum is unjustified. Moreover, continuous ReLU networks cannot uniformly approximate the generally discontinuous fS to arbitrarily small error, as asserted in Appendix F. A valid continuous construction and explicit error-transfer arguments are needed.

Theorem 5.9 does not establish robustness under the paper’s definition. Its training adversary changes only the meaningful patch along the known signal direction, whereas Definition 3.3 maximizes over the entire norm ball. Small loss against the restricted adversary does not imply small full-ball robust training error, particularly when classification relies on noise patches that the training adversary cannot modify. This breaks the claimed implication that the learned model is a CGRO classifier.

The dynamics proof contains further substantive gaps. Theorem E.12 applies sub-Gaussian concentration to a cubic polynomial of Gaussian noise; even a single cubed Gaussian is not sub-Gaussian, and different neurons share the same test noise. Additionally, Assumption 5.7 permits cα > 1/2, for which the prescribed initialization already violates the signal bound in Hypothesis E.1. Thus the clean-generalization and induction arguments require substantial repair.

The synthetic experiment uses δ = α = 10, violating the theorem’s strict δ < α condition. This permits complete deletion of the meaningful signal, so poor robust population accuracy does not validate the proposed mechanism in the claimed separable regime. The image experiments are illustrative but do not distinguish capacity limitations from optimization failure. Missing PGD step counts, step sizes, restarts, training hyperparameters, and variability across runs also limit reproducibility and confidence in the robustness measurements.

The originality of the representation lower bound is limited as stated. The existential hard distribution from the cited linear-separable setting of Li et al. (2022) already belongs to the broader class admitting polynomial-size clean classifiers. Allowing that broader class does not itself strengthen the existential result. The manuscript also does not establish a connection between this worst-case capacity barrier and the particular distribution used in its dynamics analysis.

The additional generalization bound in Theorem B.1 is unsupported under its assumptions. A constant classifier has zero input-gradient flatness, yet label-dependent losses can exhibit a positive population-minus-empirical gap with nonvanishing probability because sampled class proportions fluctuate. Appendix G also retains additive density-estimation terms that do not yield the stated bound proportional only to flatness. Together with the failures in the principal theorems, these issues prevent acceptance despite the worthwhile research objective.
